evaluations.evidence: create a new game
evaluations.rationale: Creating a new game is self-contained and does not require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: invite estimators by giving them a URL where they can access the game
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators by URL inherently requires a game to exist to generate that URL (create a new game).

evaluations.evidence: start a round by entering an item
evaluations.rationale: Starting a round requires an existing game/session context in which to start the round (create a new game).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Viewing session items requires that items exist (added in the session) and a session/game to view; it depends on adding items and having a game.

evaluations.evidence: select an item to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Selecting an item requires that items are present in a game's item list (items must be added and a game must exist).

evaluations.evidence: add an item to the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Adding an item presumes a game/session context to add the item into, so it depends on the ability to create a game.

evaluations.evidence: edit an item in the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Editing an item presumes that items and the game/session exist (items are created by adding items and a game must exist).

evaluations.evidence: delete an item from the list of items to be estimated
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an item requires items to exist in a game's item list and thus depends on item-addition and a game context.

evaluations.evidence: show all estimates immediately
evaluations.rationale: Showing estimates assumes that a round is running and estimators have joined and submitted estimates; it depends on starting rounds and joining functionality.

evaluations.evidence: accept the average of all estimates
evaluations.rationale: Accepting an average requires that estimates exist for a round (needs rounds and estimators to have submitted estimates).

evaluations.evidence: "estimate" field filled in automatically if all estimators show the same card
evaluations.rationale: Auto-filling the estimate depends on the mechanism to collect and show all estimators' cards (showing all estimates / round mechanics) and on estimators being present.

evaluations.evidence: enter the agreed-upon estimate
evaluations.rationale: Entering an agreed estimate presumes a round/item is active and that an agreement process occurred (depends on starting rounds / items).

evaluations.evidence: estimate a story we estimated earlier in the session again
evaluations.rationale: Re-estimating a previously estimated story requires that the session history of items is available (ability to view session items/history).

evaluations.evidence: import stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Importing stories is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another specific backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: copy/paste stories from a spreadsheet
evaluations.rationale: Copy/paste importing is self-contained and does not mandate another backlog story be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: browse through previous games
evaluations.rationale: Browsing previous games presumes there are stored games to browse, which requires ability to create/store games (create a new game).

evaluations.evidence: view a transcript of a game
evaluations.rationale: Viewing a transcript requires that the game and its recorded stories/estimates exist (depends on game/round creation and recording).

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a HTML file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript depends on transcripts being available (view/export transcript functionality), so it depends on the transcript/view capability.

evaluations.evidence: export a transcript of a game as a CSV file
evaluations.rationale: Exporting a transcript as CSV depends on transcripts existing/being generated (view/export transcript capability).

evaluations.evidence: delete a game
evaluations.rationale: Deleting a game presumes games exist to be deleted (depends on the ability to create/store games).

evaluations.evidence: create an account
evaluations.rationale: Account creation is self-contained and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: log in using my account name and password
evaluations.rationale: Logging in requires that an account exists (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: change my account details
evaluations.rationale: Changing account details presumes an existing account to change (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: delete my account
evaluations.rationale: Deleting an account requires that an account exists (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: see dates and times in my local timezone
evaluations.rationale: Timezone display is a standalone presentation concern and does not inherently require another backlog story to be implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: get a password reminder by email
evaluations.rationale: Password reminders presuppose an account/password exists and stored email addresses (account creation).

evaluations.evidence: select whether to have the team estimate with {0, 1/2, 1, ...} or {0, 1, 2, ...}
evaluations.rationale: Choosing the card set is a configuration option and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: invite up to 15 estimators
evaluations.rationale: Inviting estimators (with a limit) builds on the invitation mechanism (giving URL) and thus depends on the invite functionality.

evaluations.evidence: join a game by entering my name on the page I received the URL for
evaluations.rationale: Joining via URL presumes an invitation/link mechanism that provides the page/URL (invite estimators).

evaluations.evidence: see the item we're estimating
evaluations.rationale: Seeing the current item presumes a round/item has been started (start a round).

evaluations.evidence: see all items we will try to estimate this session
evaluations.rationale: Participants seeing the session's items requires that items have been added to the session (add items).

evaluations.evidence: immediately see that an estimate has been given by a specific estimator
evaluations.rationale: Noticing who has estimated presumes a running round and joined estimators to observe (start round and join functionality).

evaluations.evidence: be shown all estimates at the same time after all estimators have given their estimate
evaluations.rationale: Showing all estimates simultaneously inherently requires a round and estimators who can join and submit estimates.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate up until the last person selects a card and all are shown
evaluations.rationale: The ability to change an estimate until reveal depends on the draw/reveal mechanics (showing all estimates) and joined estimators.

evaluations.evidence: see each estimator's prior estimates for the story being estimated
evaluations.rationale: Viewing prior estimates for a story requires that prior estimates are stored and accessible (history/scrollback of prior rounds).

evaluations.evidence: see who gave what estimates during the current round
evaluations.rationale: Showing who gave which estimates requires the mechanism to reveal/record estimates for a round (show all estimates) and joined participants.

evaluations.evidence: start a two-minute countdown timer that all participants can see
evaluations.rationale: A shared countdown timer is a self-contained feature and does not inherently require another backlog story to exist first.

evaluations.evidence: two-minute timer reset itself as soon as we all play an estimate
evaluations.rationale: Auto-resetting the timer when all have played depends on both the timer feature and the mechanism to detect all estimates played (timer + reveal mechanics).

evaluations.evidence: scroll back through the stories and estimates from prior rounds
evaluations.rationale: Scrolling back through prior rounds presumes prior rounds and stored estimates exist (round/start functionality that produces prior rounds).

evaluations.evidence: always have the cards in the same order across multiple draws
evaluations.rationale: Maintaining card order across multiple draws presumes multiple draws/rounds exist and draw mechanics are implemented.

evaluations.evidence: change my estimate as long as the draw has not been completed
evaluations.rationale: Changing estimates conditional on draw completion depends on draw/reveal mechanics (showing all estimates / draw lifecycle).

evaluations.evidence: have a small thumbnail photo displayed near where my cards are played
evaluations.rationale: Displaying a thumbnail is a standalone UI feature and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have written a site which is compliant with XHTML and CSS standards
evaluations.rationale: Standards compliance is a non-dependent developer quality requirement and does not require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have a list of definitions for commonly used terms
evaluations.rationale: Providing definitions is self-contained and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have created database indexes
evaluations.rationale: Creating indexes is a developer task related to performance and does not inherently depend on another specific backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have the application function correctly in Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Firefox 1.5 and 2, and Safari 2
evaluations.rationale: Cross-browser compatibility is a developer quality goal and does not inherently depend on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the site comply with the W3C accessibility guidelines where possible
evaluations.rationale: Accessibility compliance is a standalone quality concern, not inherently dependent on other backlog stories.

evaluations.evidence: have the application respond quickly to my actions
evaluations.rationale: Performance/responsiveness is a non-functional requirement and not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: be able to use Unicode
evaluations.rationale: Unicode support is a standalone technical requirement and does not inherently require another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: see sensible and predictable URLs
evaluations.rationale: URL design is a self-contained usability requirement and does not inherently depend on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: have nice error pages when something goes wrong
evaluations.rationale: Error page design is a standalone UX requirement and is not inherently dependent on another backlog story.

evaluations.evidence: results to be stored in a non-identifiable way
evaluations.rationale: Specifying how results are stored is a requirement about storage semantics and does not inherently depend on another backlog story being implemented first.

evaluations.evidence: see some metrics on use of the game
evaluations.rationale: Requesting metrics is a reporting/analytics feature; while it needs data, it does not explicitly depend on another specific backlog story implementation.
